overview: Lanhydrock is a grand country house near Bodmin, set in around 890 acres of gardens, parkland and woods above the River Fowey, and it’s a good all-rounder for a mixed group. The house was first built in the 1620s for the Robartes family, but most of the inside was rebuilt after a fire in 1881, so what you walk round today feels like a late-Victorian family home, from the grand rooms to the servants’ quarters. The National Trust has run it since 1953.

There’s something for most people: the house if you like seeing how people lived, gardens and woodland walks for a fine day, play areas and trails for the children, and dogs are welcome across much of the estate.

expect.title: The house
expect.text: Rooms are laid out as the family and staff used them, from the long run of Victorian kitchens to the nursery. Don’t miss the Long Gallery, with a 35-metre 17th-century plaster ceiling that was conserved in 2024.

expect.title: The garden
expect.text: Formal borders, clipped yews and a croquet lawn near the house, then woodland paths above with rhododendrons and magnolias. Lanhydrock is known for its magnolias, at their peak in spring.

expect.title: Walks and cycling
expect.text: Four signed circular walks lead out across the estate, including a riverside route from Respryn Bridge where otters and kingfishers live, plus dedicated cycle trails.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: A play area by the Park Café, a family route with hands-on activities, children’s menus and seasonal trails and games.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry for non-members, with family tickets; under-5s and National Trust members go free.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Free for National Trust members. Everyone else pays by the hour or for the day, at the machines, by app or at the café or reception.

goodToKnow.label: Busy times
goodToKnow.text: It’s busiest between 11am and 2pm, when there can be queues for the house, so afternoons are often calmer.

goodToKnow.label: Bags
goodToKnow.text: Big bags and backpacks aren’t allowed in the house, but there are free lockers.

goodToKnow.label: Dogs
goodToKnow.text: Welcome on the walking trails and in most of the garden; only assistance dogs in the house and shop. Keep dogs off the cycle trails.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: Some paths suit wheelchairs and buggies, there are accessible parking bays, and an all-terrain mobility scooter can be booked for the wider estate. Satnav: PL30 4AB.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: The Park Café is by the main hub and the Stables Café is in the courtyard.

setting.note: A house to tour indoors, plus gardens and parkland

kids.note: Play area, family route and children’s activities

week.slot: Half a day to a full day
week.text: Lanhydrock works whatever the weather, which makes it a useful day to have in reserve: the house if it rains, the gardens and estate walks if it’s fine. It’s just off the A30 and A38 near Bodmin, so it’s also a good stop on your journey in or out of Cornwall.

tips: Arrive after 2pm to miss the queues for the house.
Bring bikes, or check the cycle trails: they’re a big part of the estate.
If you’re a National Trust member, bring your card: entry and parking are free.
